title: 📘 UNIT 7: GEOGRAPHIC ISSUES AND PUBLIC CONCERNS IN AFRICA
notes: 🌍 Africa faces major geographic and public concerns linked to rapid urbanization, migration, and coastal pollution.

title: 7.1 🏙️ UNPLANNED URBANIZATION
notes:
🏙️ Urbanization → the population shift from rural areas to urban areas, accompanied by a decrease in the proportion of people living in rural areas.

🏗️ Urbanization → towns and cities grow as more people live and work in them.

🌆 Unplanned urbanization → rapid urban growth that occurs without adequate planning, regulation, infrastructure, and services.

🌳 Environmental impact → expansion into forests, wetlands, and agricultural land causes habitat clearing, degradation, and fragmentation.

🗑️ Pollution → urban lifestyles consume large amounts of resources and generate increasing quantities of waste, contributing to air, water, and soil pollution.

✅ Urbanization is not inherently harmful → well-managed cities can improve economic, cultural, and social development, create employment, encourage innovation, and provide economies of scale.

⚠️ Key features of unplanned urbanization → urban sprawl, unplanned growth, land-use change, accelerated poverty, environmental degradation, poor air and water quality, insufficient water supply, and waste-disposal problems.

title: 7.1.1 🌍 CAUSES OF UNPLANNED URBANIZATION IN AFRICA
notes:
📈 Rapid urban growth → Africa is one of the fastest-urbanizing continents.

🚜 Rural–urban migration → people move to cities mainly because of employment opportunities and the expectation of better living conditions.

🏛️ Legacy of colonialism → historical colonial patterns contributed to weak and uneven urban development.

💰 Structural adjustment programs → policies associated with international institutions, including IMF programs, influenced urban development and public-sector capacity.

🌐 Neoliberalism → pressure and policies associated with developed countries contributed to changes in African economies and urban systems.

🏛️ Weak urban planning institutions → inadequate planning capacity makes it difficult to manage rapid population growth and urban expansion.

🏙️ Urban primacy → one city, often the capital, has much greater population, economic activity, and political power than the next largest city.

📊 African urbanization → much of Africa's urban expansion has been unplanned and unregulated.

title: 7.1.2 ⚠️ CONSEQUENCES OF UNPLANNED URBANIZATION
notes:
1️⃣ Slums and squatter settlements → rapid, random urban growth encourages informal residential settlements, especially where housing is scarce and expensive.

2️⃣ Poor infrastructure → infrastructure development often fails to keep pace with population growth.

🛣️ Infrastructure problems → weak roads, railways, airports, ports, electricity systems, water supply, sewage systems, and communication infrastructure.

3️⃣ 💰 Economic problems → high costs of housing, food, and transportation combined with high unemployment create serious economic pressure.

👷 Informal economy → a large share of urban employment occurs in informal activities that are generally not taxed or fully monitored by government.

4️⃣ 🏥 Health problems → inadequate sanitation, high population density, poverty, and poor infrastructure increase exposure to diseases and other health risks.

5️⃣ ⚠️ Social instability → inequality, competition for land and other scarce resources, weak governance, and lack of affordable housing can increase crime, violence, and social unrest.

🌡️ Climate-change risk → poorly planned cities are more vulnerable to floods and other extreme weather events, especially cities located near seas and waterways.

title: 7.1.3 🇪🇹 CASE STUDY: UNPLANNED URBANIZATION IN ADDIS ABABA
notes:
🇪🇹 Addis Ababa → Ethiopia's largest city and a rapidly growing urban center.

🏙️ Major challenges → unplanned urban development, inefficient land use, urban poverty, unemployment, inadequate housing, congestion, and underdeveloped infrastructure.

🏘️ Historical development → Addis Ababa developed from villages that grew into major settlements without a master plan.

🏚️ Informal settlements → developed spontaneously around major centers and often lack basic services such as water, sanitation, and waste collection.

1️⃣ Slums → highly congested settlements with deteriorated infrastructure, poor sanitation, and houses constructed from substandard materials; commonly occupied by low-income groups.

2️⃣ Squatter settlements → settlements built illegally on open spaces, farmland, steep slopes, river buffers, and roadsides without legal title deeds.

⚠️ Effects → informal settlements interfere with proper land use, make municipal service provision difficult, and encourage continued horizontal expansion of the city.

title: 7.2 🚶 MIGRATION – FACTORS AND IMPACTS ON AFRICA
notes:
🚶 Human migration → the permanent change of residence by an individual or group of people.

🏠 Internal migration → movement of people from one area to another within the same country, such as rural-to-urban migration.

🌍 International migration → movement from one country to another across an international boundary.

🕊️ Voluntary migration → movement made by choice, commonly to seek better economic opportunities or a better life.

⚠️ Forced migration → movement caused by circumstances such as war, drought, famine, natural disasters, political conflict, or expulsion.

📍 Origin → the place from which migrants leave.

🎯 Destination → the place to which migrants move.

⬆️ Push factors → conditions that encourage people to leave their place of origin.

⬇️ Pull factors → conditions that attract people to a destination.

title: 7.2.1 ⬆️ PUSH FACTORS OF MIGRATION IN AFRICA
notes:
💰 Economic push factors → poor socio-economic conditions, low wages, unemployment, and poverty.

📈 Population pressure → rapid population growth compared with available resources can increase migration pressure.

⚙️ Limited technology and employment capacity → insufficient productive capacity can restrict job creation.

🏛️ Poor governance → weak governance can encourage people to leave their areas of origin.

💼 Corruption → corruption and poor administration can contribute to migration.

⚔️ Political instability → instability, conflict, and civil strife can force or encourage people to migrate.

🌵 Environmental pressures → drought, famine, and other environmental stresses can contribute to forced migration.

title: 7.2.2 🎯 PULL FACTORS OF MIGRATION IN AFRICA
notes:
💼 Better employment → migrants may move toward places with greater job opportunities.

💵 Higher income → better wages and income prospects attract migrants.

🛡️ Greater security → safer destinations can attract people from areas affected by conflict or insecurity.

🎓 Better education → access to higher-quality educational opportunities encourages migration.

🏥 Better healthcare → improved health services can attract migrants.

🏙️ Better living conditions → improved infrastructure and services can encourage people to move to particular destinations.

title: 7.2.3 🌍 MIGRATION IN AFRICA: HISTORICAL IMPACTS
notes:
📜 Historical migration → Africa has experienced important population movements throughout its history.

⛓️ Slave migration → forced migration by European slave traders from the 16th to the 19th centuries significantly reduced the population of parts of Africa.

🗺️ Cross-border communities → some African communities are distributed across two or more modern countries because historical population movement was not limited by present political boundaries.

👥 Demographic impact → historical and contemporary migration has contributed significantly to Africa's present population distribution and demographic patterns.

🔑 Key idea → African migration has been both voluntary and forced and has occurred internally and internationally.

title: 7.3 🌊 COASTAL POLLUTION IN AFRICA
notes:
🌊 Coastal pollution → contamination of coastal and marine environments by pollutants originating from coastal and inland human activities.

🏭 Major sources → municipal sewage, industrial waste, ship waste, dumping at sea, cargo handling, seabed and ocean-floor exploration, oil spills, and pollutants transported from inland areas.

🚽 Major cause → discharge of municipal sewage and industrial waste into coastal waters or estuaries through inadequate disposal facilities.

🌊 River connection → pollutants discharged into rivers far inland can eventually reach the sea.

☣️ Major pollutant classes → decomposable organic materials, heavy metals and toxic substances, non-toxic inorganic substances, and pathogenic organisms.

🏙️ Growing threat → population growth, urbanization, and industrial development along African coasts are increasing coastal pollution.

title: 7.3.1 🛢️ MAJOR CAUSES AND EFFECTS OF COASTAL POLLUTION
notes:
🛢️ Oil pollution → oil leaks, accidental spills from ships, oil drilling, and mineral extraction contaminate marine environments.

🚢 Shipping pollution → ships can release rubbish, sewage, and bilgewater into the marine environment.

🌾 Agricultural runoff → agricultural and urban runoff can carry nutrients and pollutants into coastal waters.

🏭 Industrial waste → industrial discharge introduces harmful substances into rivers, estuaries, and coastal waters.

🌿 Wetland and mangrove destruction → removing natural filters allows more sediment, nutrients, and waste to accumulate in coastal environments.

🐟 Effects on marine life → habitat destruction, over-fishing, pollution, biodiversity loss, and disruption of ecosystem functioning.

👨‍👩‍👧 Human effects → pollution can threaten human health, livelihoods, fisheries, and coastal resources.

🌍 Land-based pollution → many marine pollution problems originate from human activities far inland and reach the ocean through rivers, watersheds, and air.

title: 7.3.2 ♻️ PLASTIC POLLUTION IN AFRICAN SEAS AND OCEANS
notes:
♻️ Plastic pollution → one of the major threats to marine and coastal ecosystems.

🐟 Environmental effects → loss of biodiversity, damage to ecosystems, and disruption of marine ecosystem functioning.

👨‍⚕️ Human effects → can threaten human health and coastal livelihoods.

🌊 Pathway → plastic waste can enter rivers through littering, poor waste management, and overflowing landfills before reaching the ocean.

🇿🇦 South Africa example → a large proportion of marine pollution originates from land-based sources, showing the strong connection between land management and ocean pollution.

🤝 Solution principle → plastic pollution requires coordinated action involving governments, communities, businesses, environmental organizations, and other stakeholders.

title: 📚 UNIT 7 SUMMARY
notes:
🏙️ Unplanned urbanization → rapid urban growth without adequate planning and infrastructure, producing problems such as slums, poor services, environmental degradation, poverty, health risks, and social instability.

🚶 Migration → permanent movement of people and may be internal or international, voluntary or forced.

⬆️ Push factors → poverty, unemployment, low wages, poor governance, conflict, political instability, drought, and other pressures.

🎯 Pull factors → better employment, higher income, security, education, healthcare, and living conditions.

🌊 Coastal pollution → contamination caused by sewage, industrial waste, oil, plastics, shipping activities, agricultural runoff, and other pollutants.

🔗 Interconnected problems → population growth, urbanization, industrialization, migration, environmental degradation, and weak infrastructure can reinforce one another.

🤝 Sustainable solutions → effective urban planning, strong governance, improved infrastructure, public awareness, environmental management, coordinated institutions, and multi-stakeholder cooperation.

title: 📝 UNIT 7: EXAM QUICK REVIEW
notes:
🔹 Urbanization = population shift from rural to urban areas.

🔹 Unplanned urbanization = rapid urban growth without adequate planning and regulation.

🔹 Major causes = rural–urban migration, colonial legacy, structural adjustment pressures, neoliberal policies, and weak urban planning institutions.

🔹 Major consequences = slums, poor infrastructure, economic problems, health problems, social instability, and environmental degradation.

🔹 Urban primacy = dominance of one city over other cities in population, economic activity, and political power.

🔹 Internal migration = movement within a country.

🔹 International migration = movement across national borders.

🔹 Voluntary migration = migration by choice.

🔹 Forced migration = migration caused by conflict, drought, famine, disasters, or other pressures.

🔹 Push factors = conditions that drive people away.

🔹 Pull factors = conditions that attract people toward a destination.

🔹 Coastal pollution = contamination of coastal and marine environments.

🔹 Major coastal pollutants = sewage, industrial waste, oil, plastics, ship waste, agricultural runoff, and toxic substances.

🔹 Main solution principle = prevention, proper waste management, effective planning, environmental protection, and coordinated action.
